claims.text: Local fluctuations in short-range chemical order create regions with locally reduced stacking-fault energy.
Local chemical order alters the balance among dislocation slip, twinning, stacking-fault formation, and deformation-induced phase transformation.
Differences in short-range order govern strain-hardening and ductility differences across Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets relative to the equiatomic quinary alloy.
The investigated equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and selected quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Localized short-range order modulates the stacking-fault-energy landscape and promotes stacking faults and twin-boundary nucleation.
Regions with enhanced short-range order have lower local stacking-fault energies.
Lower local stacking-fault energy favors partial-dislocation mechanisms, including twinning and stacking-fault formation, over ordinary dislocation slip.
Chemical variation can promote three-dimensional stacking-fault networks associated with FCC-to-HCP transformation.
A shift toward stacking-fault and twinning mechanisms changes macroscopic strain-hardening behavior.
Alloys with enhanced short-range order will develop a higher density of stacking faults and twin boundaries during straining.
The higher stacking-fault and twin density will produce increased strain-hardening and a more favorable strength-ductility balance than in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Alloys without pronounced short-range order will deform predominantly by dislocation slip and exhibit lower strain-hardening.
The proposed mechanism applies only to alloys that remain single-phase FCC after processing.
The hypothesis may cease to apply when significant FCC-to-HCP transformation occurs.
Substantial changes in processing conditions may change chemical order and mechanical behavior enough to invalidate comparisons made under the controlled regime.

Failure to find a statistically significant correlation among short-range order, stacking-fault or twin formation, and macroscopic mechanical-property differences would falsify the proposed governing role of short-range order.
